newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut prison guards demand pay hike.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut prison guards demand pay hike.

text.p: Thousands of off-duty prison guards and their supporters marched on the state capitol on Wednesday to demand more money from lawmakers.
Organizers said the day-long rally was to protest the state's rejection of the prison guards' arbitrated contract award, which was shot down last week by the state senate.
Hundreds of prison guards arrived in the morning, forcing capitol police to beef up security.
Leaders of the 5,000-member guards' union told reporters that they deserved a raise because they had been without one for four years.
However, Gov. John Rowland (R) and Senate Majority Leader George Jepsen (D) said Wednesday that the state would not budge.
"We felt this contract was too generous, too lucrative," Jepsen told Reuters. "It put about a $30 million hole in our state budget."
"The prison guards' unit is one of the largest in the state, and they're a pretty vocal group," he said.
"The demonstration was aggressive and loud, but it was peaceful," Jepsen said.
"We're just asking them to accept a contract that more closely resembles the pattern of contracts that every other state employee has accepted either through negotiation or arbitration."
Jepsen said the guards should come back to the negotiating table, because there are only three weeks left in the legislative session.
